trajectory.development: Book 24 (Working Book text, agent-proposed): the labour gap is first met by people rather than by a schedule, and a generation that refuses to be counted is asked to give back the water before it is owed. The Special Draw Right's review point falls here, and the Right is conditional on training apprentices from outside the lineage.
trajectory.becomes_available: Since Book 20 lineage crews have carried channel repair under the Right while households meet the rota (E1). Book 24 is where that carrying is first tested, so the Right's condition becomes a live question.
trajectory.changes: Turns a settled arrangement into a conditional one under review, so later Books can show consequences of the mechanism rather than restate that it exists.

trajectory.development: Book 25 repeats five of Book 24's six citing elements word for word, with matching source hashes (E14). No development specific to Book 25 is recorded.
trajectory.becomes_available: Book 24's account of the labour gap and of the Right's condition (s1), which the Book 25 entries restate.
trajectory.changes: Nothing new is recorded. The copied E11 still says Book 24 is where the gap is first met, so Book 25 points back to Book 24 instead of standing on its own. It needs its own development before it can be a stage.

trajectory.development: Apprentices from outside the lineage are trained under the Right's condition, and the generation that came of age after Book 20 is brought into the labour for the first time, held to the lineage's craft standard. Conditional proposal; no new people or factions are named.
trajectory.becomes_available: Once s1 has made the condition a review, training outside the lineage can be shown rather than asserted (E7). The generation that has never seen the labour (E6) can then take part in it.
trajectory.changes: The mechanism shifts from custody by one lineage to shared performance. The lineage's craft guard (E3) becomes the standard trainees must meet rather than a reason to keep the labour closed.

trajectory.development: A public capability record, separate from debt, tally and aggregate balance, is used to show who can repair. Repair is recorded as capability rather than as obligation or count. Conditional proposal.
trajectory.becomes_available: Trained repairers from s3 exist, and Book 24 already exports the new record kind, which says who can repair rather than who owes (E5).
trajectory.changes: Repair becomes a public fact rather than a rota entry, which changes what the Right's condition means in practice. It may let the uncounted cohort give back without first being counted (inferred from E5).

trajectory.development: The cohort that now practises both counted and uncounted return may claim standing in how the valley coordinates channel work. This is conditional on s3. E8 is hypothetical and names no body that would grant standing, so the grantor is an open choice for a later Book.
trajectory.becomes_available: Counted and uncounted practice now crosses generations (E4). The cohort has practised both only if s3 happens, and s4 gives the standing claim something public to be judged against.
trajectory.changes: The mechanism moves from performing the labour to coordinating it, so the question of who keeps the channels becomes a question of who may decide how they are kept.

relations.reason: The condition set at s1 gives training under the Right its reason. Training can happen without the review, but the review makes it a test.

The lineage guards craft standards and fears dilution by untrained gift-hands (E3, an agent inference), while the Right requires training outsiders (E7). Training in s3 therefore meets resistance from the lineage the Right depends on.
The standing in s5 is claimed by a cohort that practises both counted and uncounted return, and only s3 brings that practice about. Without s3 there is no such cohort to claim standing.
The capability record can be exported without trained outsiders, but then it would list only lineage members. s3 gives it content beyond the lineage.
A public record of who can repair gives the standing claim in s5 something to be judged by. Standing can be claimed without it, but not on evidence.
Book 25's recorded text restates Book 24, so its place after s1 is ordering only. No development in Book 25 depends on s1 beyond the repeated words.

alternative_paths.ordering: Train outside apprentices (s3) before the capability record (s4) is used, and let the record report only trained repairers.
alternative_paths.effect: The record becomes a test of the Right's condition rather than a register of existing repairers, so it does not repeat the lineage rota in a new form.

alternative_paths.ordering: Move from s1 to the standing question (s5) without s3, so a cohort claims coordination on the strength of its own return.
alternative_paths.effect: The standing lacks the training the Right requires, and the lineage's stake (E3) goes unanswered. The mechanism becomes a contest over authority rather than a development of the labour.

alternative_paths.ordering: Keep the labour with lineage crews and households through the next Books (no s3), and let the restated Book 25 text stand as the only development.
alternative_paths.effect: The Right's condition is left untested. If the reading in E3 holds, the Right is exposed, and the mechanism becomes a repeated rota, which is the repetition the question asks to avoid.

opportunities.text: Training outsiders can meet the lineage's craft standard instead of ending it. The standard becomes what trainees are judged against, which gives the lineage a reason to teach as well as to guard. The lineage stake is an agent inference (E3).

A public record of repair capability may let the uncounted cohort give back the water without entering the counted ledger. The labour gap could then be met without asking the cohort to be counted first.

Making standing depend on a public record shifts the question of who keeps the channels from whose debt is owed to whose repair can be seen. That is a change of register rather than another round of the same labour.

reader_experience: Book 24 gives the first meeting with the labour gap as people's labour, and Book 25 needs a second angle rather than a copy. Later stages move the reader from who carries the water, to who may teach it, to who may decide how the channels are kept. If the later stages never arrive, Book 24 still keeps the gap met and the review point held. Keep the wonder and belonging the Story Vision asks for (E2, excerpt, which warns against 'a generic escalating-villain epic') rather than escalating at each stage.
open_decisions: Whether Book 25 gets its own development or the restated text is cut as repetition (E14).
Whether any body grants the cohort standing in channel coordination. The record names none (E8).
Whether the Right's training condition is shown in a proposed Book or kept as an open tension (E3, E7).
Whether the public capability record is a new record kind or is folded into existing tallies (E5).
uncertainty: The E2 Story Vision excerpt is truncated, so the full constraints on victories and experience are not seen.
The lineage stake (E3, E9) is an agent inference and the Book 25 derivation (E6, E12) is derived. E4 carries unknown_legacy status.
E5 and E11 are truncated, so the full wording of the capability record is not shown.
